Hi Product Hunt, I'm William! I made Rill because I want to always stay in the flow.

As an ADHD, I never liked code-switching. My best ideas for work come when I'm supposedly not working at all: watching something for fun, reading things and following a rabbit hole, looking at how someone else solved a problem. Then when an idea hit me, I'd have to stop, switch to coding agents, find the project and explain it all, and most of the time I just didn't. [...] Rill is my way of removing that code-switching. It's a browser with your Claude Code or Codex working alongside you. When something on a page gives you an idea, you say so right there, and an agent starts on it in the right project. You don't have to spend time looking for the right folder, rephrasing everything you just saw on the web, and you don't switch in and out of work mode. The work goes on with you in the flow.

This matters now more than ever. Agents have shortened the distance between ideas to output near zero. So the bottleneck is capturing the idea at the moment you have it. That moment is nearly always while you're taking something in, and that is what a browser is for. [...] Rill is a free AI-native browser. It's WebKit-based, which means it's native to Mac. And it runs on the Claude Code or Codex plan you already have, so you don't have to buy a new subscription for all of its agentic capabilities.c

How do you keep an idea today when it shows up at the wrong time?

# FAQ

## Technical requirements​

### Why does macOS say "Rill cannot be opened because it is from an unidentified developer"?​

This occurs when the Rill binary is downloaded via the browser. You need to change the permissions to make it executable and remove it from Apple's developer identification quarantine.

The CLI commands below will help you do that:

`chmod a+x rill  
xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ./rill`

### Why am I seeing "This macOS version is not supported. Please upgrade"?​

Rill uses DuckDB internally, which requires a newer macOS version.
Please upgrade your macOS version to 10.14 or higher.

### Which browsers work best with Rill?​ [...] ### Which browsers work best with Rill?​

Rill is optimized for Google Chrome. While other browsers may work, we recommend using the latest version of Chrome for the most reliable experience when accessing Rill Developer or Rill Cloud dashboards.

## Rill Developer​

### What is Rill Developer?​

Rill Developer is a local application used to preview your project and make any necessary changes before deploying to Rill Cloud. For more information, please review our documentation. Within Rill Developer, you can ingest new datasets, transform the sources into models, build a metrics layer, and finally visualize your data in an explore dashboard. This preview allows you to develop your project before deploying or updating an existing deployment in Rill Cloud.

AI Workflow Automation

Rill is an AI-native browser built around the Claude Code and Codex you already use. Browse normally, then press ⌘E on any page to turn what you're looking at into a task for your agent. Rill finds the right project, passes along the context, and the agent works while you keep browsing. It also sorts your tabs into themes, turns your history into days you can search, and brings every project your agents are working on into one place. Free, on the plan you already have.
